chapter_title: The Chapter of Fasting, for it engenders a Host of Angels
chapter_note: This kephalaion is dominated by hagiographic dialogue frame plus institutional/pastoral material about fasting practice, ecclesial leadership responsibility, and avoiding sin in directing church works (building, alms). Even the seemingly “mechanistic” claim about fasting ‘engendering seven angels’ is anchored to church categories (elect, catechumens, lord’s day) and presented inside a first-person administrative narrative, not as impersonal cosmos→cosmos correspondential exposition. No recoverable pre-compilation substrate layer is visible in this excerpt.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic scene-setting (“Once again… apostle… congregation… disciple”), plus institutional categories (elect/catechumens, lord’s day). The angel-count claim is embedded in a framed exchange and tied to church practice rather than impersonal cosmological mapping.
Administrative/institutional self-report (“became leader… elect… church… head”), not systematic cosmological instruction.
Quantifying angels produced by fasts, but entirely keyed to ecclesial schedule (three lord’s days) and community roles; narrative/accounting voice rather than core cosmological architecture.
Continues the institutional calculation and personal gratitude for ‘profit’ achieved in church fast-days; no cosmos-internal correspondential system is being expounded.
Conscience/anxiety over sin in commanding church construction/necessities; direct self-questioning and church ordinance language marks institutional application rather than substrate exposition.

Petition formula and address (“I entreat you, my master… perform this grace… release me”), with institutional role (“power [of] protection of the gods and angels”) and brotherhood setting; clearly part of the dialogue apparatus.
Narrative transition (“Then, when the apostle had heard…”)—pure frame connective.
Dialogue attribution (“The apostle says…”) plus admonitory reasoning addressed to the disciple; not impersonal cosmological teaching and remains within the hagiographic Q&A format.
Second-person exhortation and motivational eschatology (“land of rest… children of the living”) used to keep the disciple in his entrusted work; application-voice dominates.
Promissory encouragement and direct address (“it will be told to you… I will… so that you wish…”); pastoral exhortation rather than system description.
Institutional argument about who will do ‘divine work’ if leaders withdraw; ethical/pastoral reasoning about responsibility and sin.
Imperatives and assignment language (“you do the work… do not strive to ask exemption”); explicit application voice.
Programmatic valuation of preaching/building the church over private edification; explicitly ecclesial and comparative exhortation.
Directly about ‘building a church’ and ‘alms’ and the fear of sin in church work—fully institutional application.
Moral casuistry about speaking/commanding for selfish need vs church need; sin language and behavioral regulation, not cosmological mechanism.
Direct commission (“I assign to you… preach… build the church of God”); pastoral/institutional directive.
Formulaic closing response and homage (“heard these things… paid homage… My master…”), sealing the dialogue frame.
